definition: The time an exponentially decaying quantity takes to fall to half its value; for $N_{0}\mathrm{e}^{-kt}$ with $N_{0} > 0$ and $k > 0$ it is $\frac{\ln 2}{k}$, the same whatever the starting amount.
A function $f(x) = \frac{L}{1 + C\mathrm{e}^{-kx}}$ with $L, C, k > 0$, used to model restricted growth: its S-shaped graph rises almost exponentially at first, then slows and levels off towards $L$.
In a logistic model $f(x) = \frac{L}{1 + C\mathrm{e}^{-kx}}$ with $L, C, k > 0$, the value $L$: the horizontal asymptote $y = L$, a long-term limit the quantity approaches but never reaches.

Informally, a function whose graph has no breaks or jumps on an interval, so it can be drawn there without lifting your pen; a piecewise function is continuous at a joining point when the rules on both sides give the same value there.
